data.name: Booty Diver
data.detailed_description:
Grab That Booty!


Take a dive into the perilous depths of the ocean as you seek sunken treasure while battling creatures who guard their treasure as you manage your precious air supply.

  • 25 Action Packed Levels
  • 5 Boss Encounters
  • 3 Difficulty Modes
  • Unlockables Based On Difficulty Modes
  • Full Controller Support
  • Retro Inspired Art Style
  • Chiptune Soundtrack
  • Arcade Style Action
  • Progression Saving After Each Boss Battle
  • Fun For All Ages

Booty Diver is a retro arcade action game based on Atari/Nintendo games of yesteryear. The game take's a lot of inspiration from the unreleased Atari 2600 title Aquaventure. As the titular "Diver" you traverse 5 different regions of the ocean seeking out sunken treasure (Booty) guarded by King Poseidon ,and his guardians.
These dives will not be a simple splash and grab though as you must manage a limited air supply while battling Poseidon's minions which include Starfish, Octopi, and etc. Do not threat though as the "Diver" has a few means to defend himself with his short range diver's knife ,and his trusty harpoon gun.

There are 5 different regions of the ocean where you take 5 dive's per a region with each being capped off by a battle with a guardian. Some dives may require a bit more work than just battling through the monsters of the deep as you may need solve various unique challenges. After each difficulty mode play-thru it offers an unlock which gives incentive to return to the ocean depths one more time on a higher difficulty setting.

The game offers full controller support with Xbox(360/One), and Dualshock 4 controllers which is the recommended way to play the game. Keyboard controls are also available although not recommended way to play. Each level has it's own chiptune soundtrack with the exception of the boss battles.


*****PLEASE NOTE*****

The reviews listed are from the Nintendo Wii U versions of the game pre-patch. The Steam edition of the game has all the enhancements made to the game via patching.

reviews.review:
Game does what it says and lives up to it's description. There seems to be a repetitiveness that doesn't stick. simple sound over and over tends to ruin the ears but not completely destroy. 

There is a lot of potential if the game continues to be updated but as it, the game does what it says. no bugs, no real issues. just basic straight up nes scratchin.
